chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who buys merchandise with a dirham while it is deficient by a grain or something like that. May he give it to the one from whom he buys without informing him that it is deficient? He said: No, unless it is like this al-Waḍāḥiyyah, which is permissible, just as it is accepted among us by count.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمِ: a dirham coin used as payment in a commercial transaction
key_terms.الْحَبَّةَ: a small unit or grain indicating slight deficiency
key_terms.الْمَبِيعَ: the commodity or item being sold
key_terms.الْوَضَاحِيَّةِ: a known type of coin accepted in circulation by convention
key_terms.عَدَدًا: by count rather than by weighing each individual coin
key_terms.يَنْقُصُ: being deficient or underweight in value or measure

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to use a deficient coin in a sale without informing the seller?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on using deficient coinage in transactions. A person may not pay with a coin that is underweight without informing the seller, except in cases where such coins are commonly recognized and accepted by count in the marketplace.
